items.stem: You need to lay out a page with both rows and columns that align in two dimensions. Which is the best fit?

options.rationale: Correct: Grid is designed for two-dimensional row-and-column layouts.
Flexbox is primarily one-dimensional; two-dimensional alignment is awkward with it.
Floats are a legacy technique ill-suited to structured 2D layout.
Absolute positioning does not create a flexible responsive grid.

items.explanation: Correct: Grid is designed for two-dimensional row-and-column layouts.

items.stem: Why prefer CSS custom properties over hard-coded colour values in a design system?

options.text: They allow central theming and run-time changes from one source of truth
options.rationale: Correct: custom properties let tokens drive the whole system and support theming.

options.text: They make the CSS file invalid

options.rationale: Custom properties participate in the cascade normally.

options.text: They only work in print styles
options.rationale: They work across all media, not just print.

items.explanation: Correct: custom properties let tokens drive the whole system and support theming.

items.stem: Which TWO practices keep design-system CSS maintainable? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: predictable names make styles discoverable and safe to change.
Correct: controlled specificity avoids brittle overrides.
!important escalates specificity wars and harms maintainability.
Deep coupling makes CSS fragile and hard to reuse.

items.explanation: Correct: consistent naming and deliberate specificity/layering keep design-system CSS maintainable.
